A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPPr research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the expanded and reorganized later version.

before.justification: v1 reports original DAPPr classification, uncertainty estimation, OOD detection, regularizer ablation, and approximation-validation results, alongside attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds classification and question-answering experiments, calibration analyses, further ablations, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The posterior projection, Dirichlet approximation, closed-form maximizer, softplus-plus-one parameterization, regularizer, uncertainty scores, and loss pseudocode remain unchanged. New experimental backbones and newly documented regularization schedules do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds TinyImageNet as a supervised 200-class task, beyond its existing OOD role, and adds ImageNet classification. It also extends evaluation to Mistral-7B on OpenBookQA, with ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, and CommonsenseQA as OOD datasets. MNIST and CIFAR-10-C remain present in Appendix E.

E2.justification: The CIFAR comparison adds DUQ, KL-PN, RKL-PN, PostNet, NatPN, RSNN, and ensembles. The fine-grained comparison adds DUQ, KL-PN, RKL-PN, PostNet, and NatPN. IB-EDL participates in the new LLM comparison. These substantially broaden evaluated comparators; MC Dropout/MC Drop and RS-NN/RSNN are matched as renamed methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include TinyImageNet training with a 95/5 split, ImageNet evaluation using frozen MAE ViT-B/16 features and a trained classifier, and Mistral-7B fine-tuning with ECE, NLL, and OOD AUROC reporting. Appendix F introduces a separate batch-128 runtime comparison. Retained experiments' stated splits and budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds reliability diagrams testing calibration on CIFAR-10 and Stanford Dogs, regularizer ablations on CIFAR-10-LT and CIFAR-100, and memory/runtime comparisons testing efficiency. Existing regularization sensitivity, training-size, evidence-distribution, corruption, and leave-one-out approximation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report predictive results as mean ± standard deviation over five random seeds. Added predictive experiments retain this practice, while cost measurements are averaged over five runs. No revised run count for existing experiments, new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Matched original table entries remain numerically unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results for new comparators, tasks, calibration, ablations, and efficiency. Examples include 89.47±0.6 OpenBookQA accuracy and 63.43±0.1 ImageNet accuracy. Added CIFAR ensemble rows exceed single-model DAPPr accuracy; on OpenBookQA, DAPPr's ECE of 3.11 exceeds IB-EDL's better 2.27.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, high-capacity approximation, Proposition 1, and Appendix A proof are retained. Changes to conditioning notation and added explanations of Bayesian prediction, initialization, and applicability do not introduce a new formal result or substantively revise the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the performance claim from state-of-the-art EDL methods to second-order predictors generally, and the introduction explicitly includes LLM uncertainty quantification. The central contributions of possibilistic projection, tractable Dirichlet approximation, and computational efficiency remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused explanations connecting the regularizer to minimum commitment and suppression of unsupported class evidence. It acknowledges that the parameterization precludes exact uninformative initialization, explains ordinary random initialization, and discusses reduced applicability in low-capacity settings. These qualify and elaborate the existing interpretation without replacing it.

D1.justification: Appendix C and Table 7 newly disclose warmup and linear regularization schedules, alongside retained coefficient values; this does not establish that earlier experiments changed. v2 also supplies new dataset/model configurations, baseline-tuning information, and V100 hardware details for timing. The abstract changes code availability from promised to reported available.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational possibility-theory references and citations supporting the new LLM, dataset, and MAE experiments. It explicitly positions DAPPr as building on Hieu et al.'s possibilistic foundation, already cited in v1, and expands the EDL comparison in Appendix B. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The introduction and portions of Sections 4.1–4.4 receive localized rewriting and explanatory expansion. MNIST and corruption discussions move into Appendix E, and appendix headings become more specific. The main six-section narrative and much of the existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview diagram, a pipeline diagram, reliability plots, and tables for new benchmarks, ablations, and efficiency. Existing comparison tables expand, Table 6 is transposed into a compact layout, and MNIST and corruption tables move to the appendix. These substantially change the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's generality, calibration, and efficiency through broader comparator families, larger-scale classification, LLM evaluation, reliability diagrams, and measured computational costs. Newly disclosed schedules and implementation details also improve reproducibility. Some prose remains overbroad, such as the unqualified best-CIFAR-accuracy statement despite higher ensemble scores in Table 1, but this limited issue does not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
